# Abstract {.unnumbered}

::: {.abstract-box}
**Aim.** The Asian longhorned tick, *Haemaphysalis longicornis*, is an invasive vector of
*Theileria orientalis* and other pathogens in Australia. We projected how climate change will alter
its climatic suitability across continental Australia and Tasmania. We also re-evaluated an earlier
projection analysis and corrected its errors.

**Location.** Continental Australia and Tasmania.

**Methods.** A MaxEnt consensus model, calibrated across the native and invaded ranges (including
New Zealand and the Pacific islands) and validated by leave-one-region-out transfer, was projected to
four Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP1-2.6 to SSP5-8.5) and four periods to 2100, using ten CMIP6
GCMs screened for climate sensitivity and independence. Future bioclimatic and aridity predictors were
derived from each GCM's monthly climate with the same formulations as the training data. We quantified
gains, losses and persistence of suitable climate; extrapolation (MESS, ExDet) and clamping; the
contributions of temperature and moisture to change; and the partitioning of uncertainty among
emissions scenario, GCM and SDM (30 bootstrap replicates).

**Results.** The earlier analysis projected a model that failed to transfer between continents. Its
future aridity index exceeded its theoretical maximum across 10–68% of the land area, which explains
most of the reported extrapolation. In the corrected projections, suitable area in Australia declines
by 12% by 2021–2040 and by 20%, 24%, 34% and 45% by 2081–2100 under SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, SSP3-7.0 and
SSP5-8.5, respectively. Losses occur at the warm and dry margins in Queensland, New South Wales,
Victoria, South Australia and Western Australia; Tasmania remains almost entirely suitable, and gains
are negligible. Warming is the main driver, followed by increased evaporative demand. Projected losses
lie within analogue climates. The GCM dominates uncertainty until mid-century and the emissions
scenario thereafter. The share of known Australian localities that remain suitable falls from 82% to
42–67% by 2081–2100.

**Main conclusions.** Climate change will contract the Australian range of *H. longicornis* towards
a persistent core in south-eastern New South Wales, eastern and southern Victoria and Tasmania, where
the tick and its pathogens will remain long-term problems for livestock. Part of this contraction has
probably already occurred. Physically consistent future predictors and sensitivity-screened GCM
ensembles are essential for credible projections.
:::

**Keywords:** *Haemaphysalis longicornis*; Asian longhorned tick; climate change; CMIP6; species distribution model; MaxEnt; extrapolation; uncertainty partitioning; biosecurity; Australia; Tasmania

# Introduction

The Asian longhorned tick, *Haemaphysalis longicornis* Neumann, is a three-host ixodid tick native to
temperate East Asia that has been established in eastern Australia for more than a century
[@hoogstraal1968; @heath2016]. It is the principal vector of *Theileria orientalis* Ikeda, the cause
of oriental theileriosis outbreaks in Australian cattle [@kamau2011], and
in East Asia it transmits severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus and many other pathogens
[@yu2011; @zhao2020]. Like other ixodid ticks, it spends most of its life off the host, so its
distribution is closely tied to climate: temperature governs development, questing and overwinter
survival, and the atmospheric moisture balance governs the survival of non-feeding stages
[@needham1991; @ogden2016]. In a companion analysis we showed that a MaxEnt consensus model calibrated
across the native and invaded ranges, and selected explicitly for its ability to transfer between
regions, reproduces the Australian distribution of the tick without using any Oceanian records
(`code_6`). That model is calibrated on records from the native range, North America, Australia,
New Zealand and the Pacific islands, but its projections are restricted to continental Australia and
Tasmania. Current climatic suitability is concentrated on the humid, thermally equable eastern
seaboard of Australia and in Tasmania, and is bounded inland by aridity and continental temperature
regimes and to the north by heat.

Australia is warming, and southern Australia is projected to become drier, particularly in the
cool season [@grose2020]. Because the current distribution of *H. longicornis* is limited by heat in
the north, aridity inland and cold in the south and at altitude, climate change could plausibly
contract its range at its warm and dry margins and expand it at its cool margins. Where these changes
occur, and how confidently they can be projected, matters for livestock industries and for
surveillance and control programmes.

Projecting a species distribution model (SDM) into future climates adds problems to those of
calibrating it. First, every predictor must be derivable from climate-model output in a way that is
consistent with the data used to train the model; derived indices that are approximated by ad hoc
scaling can move outside the range of physically possible values. Second, the choice of global
climate models (GCMs) is not neutral: several CMIP6 models have equilibrium climate sensitivities
(ECS) above the range assessed as very likely by the IPCC, and ensembles that include many of these
"hot" models overstate warming for a given emissions pathway [@forster2021; @hausfather2022]. Third,
future climates may be outside the range of conditions used to calibrate the model, either for single
variables or for combinations of variables, where correlative predictions are unreliable
[@elith2010; @owens2013; @mesgaran2014]. Fourth, projections carry uncertainty from the emissions
scenario, the GCM and the SDM itself, and the SDM component is often the largest yet the least often
reported [@buisson2010; @thuiller2019]. Finally, area estimates depend on the suitability threshold
and on correct accounting for latitude-dependent cell areas.

An earlier iteration of this project (`code_2`, Steps 8–10) projected the previous ("v2") model to
two emissions scenarios, two periods and five GCMs, and reported contractions of 19–45% in suitable
area. Here we re-examine that analysis critically and repeat it on the improved model. Our aims were
to: (i) identify and correct methodological problems in the previous projections and quantify their
effects; (ii) project the transfer-validated consensus model to four Shared Socioeconomic Pathways
(SSPs), four 20-year periods to 2100 and an ensemble of ten GCMs screened for climate sensitivity;
(iii) quantify gains, losses and persistence of suitable climate by jurisdiction, and the fate of
the localities where the tick is currently known; (iv) attribute projected changes to temperature
and moisture; (v) assess extrapolation and partition projection uncertainty among emissions
scenario, GCM and SDM; and (vi) translate the projections into categories relevant to surveillance
and management.


# Methods

## Evaluation of the previous future-climate analysis

We reviewed the code and outputs of the previous projection workflow (`code_2/08_future_climate_data_v2.qmd`,
`09_future_projections_v2.qmd`, `10_visualization_results_v2.qmd`), re-ran its key calculations where
the intermediate files were available, and compared them with the corrected analysis described below.
The problems found fall into five groups (@supptbl-v2): (1) the model being projected; (2) how future
values of derived predictors were calculated; (3) the composition of the GCM ensemble and the
scenario design; (4) how suitable area and extrapolation were computed and reported; and (5) the
absence of any attribution or uncertainty partitioning. The effect of each correctable problem is
quantified in the Results.

```{r}
#| label: baseline-model
#| code-summary: "Show code: baseline consensus model and lambda-based prediction"
occ <- read_csv(file.path(proc_v2, "occurrences_with_climate.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(region = if_else(region == "Other", "East_Asia", region))
env_all <- rast(file.path(proc_v2, "env_all_global.tif"))
# Training background of code_6 (identical to code_3); predictor values re-extracted at full precision from the source grid
bg_train <- read_csv(file.path(proc_v6, "background_train.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |> dplyr::select(lon, lat, region)
bg_train <- bind_cols(bg_train, terra::extract(env_all, as.matrix(bg_train[, c("lon", "lat")])))
fm <- readRDS(file.path(proc_v6, "final_consensus_models.rds"))
members <- fm$members; m_final <- fm$models
kr3 <- readRDS(file.path(base_dir, "outputs_6", "key_results.rds"))
sel_vars <- kr3$sel_vars
temp_vars  <- c("bio1", "bio2")
moist_vars <- setdiff(sel_vars, temp_vars)

# Vectorised MaxEnt cloglog prediction from the fitted lambdas (identical to maxent.jar; verified below)
parse_lambdas <- function(m) {
  lam  <- m@lambdas
  meta <- lam[grepl("^(linearPredictorNormalizer|densityNormalizer|numBackgroundPoints|entropy)", lam)]
  mv   <- setNames(as.numeric(sub(".*, ", "", meta)), sub(",.*", "", meta))
  f    <- do.call(rbind, strsplit(lam[!lam %in% meta], ", "))
  f    <- data.frame(feature = f[, 1], lambda = as.numeric(f[, 2]), min = as.numeric(f[, 3]), max = as.numeric(f[, 4]))
  list(f = f[f$lambda != 0, ], lpn = mv[["linearPredictorNormalizer"]], dn = mv[["densityNormalizer"]],
       H = mv[["entropy"]])
}
mx_cloglog <- function(L, x, clamp = TRUE) {
  s <- numeric(nrow(x))
  for (j in seq_len(nrow(L$f))) {
    ft <- L$f$feature[j]; lo <- L$f$min[j]; hi <- L$f$max[j]
    val <- if (startsWith(ft, "'")) { v <- x[[substring(ft, 2)]]; ifelse(v <= lo, 0, (v - lo) / (hi - lo)) }   # hinge
      else if (startsWith(ft, "`")) { v <- x[[substring(ft, 2)]]; ifelse(v >= hi, 0, (hi - v) / (hi - lo)) }  # reverse hinge
      else if (grepl("\\^2$", ft)) (x[[sub("\\^2$", "", ft)]]^2 - lo) / (hi - lo)                           # quadratic
      else if (grepl("\\*", ft)) { p <- strsplit(ft, "\\*")[[1]]; (x[[p[1]]] * x[[p[2]]] - lo) / (hi - lo) } # product
      else (x[[ft]] - lo) / (hi - lo)                                                                       # linear
    if (clamp) val <- pmin(pmax(val, 0), 1)
    s <- s + L$f$lambda[j] * val
  }
  1 - exp(-exp(L$H) * exp(s - L$lpn) / L$dn)
}
ens_pred <- function(Ls, x, clamp = TRUE) rowMeans(sapply(Ls, mx_cloglog, x = x, clamp = clamp))
L_final <- lapply(m_final, parse_lambdas)

p_occ   <- ens_pred(L_final, occ)
thr_p10 <- unname(quantile(p_occ, 0.10))          # identical to code_3/code_6 threshold
thr_mss <- kr3$thr_mss
p_java  <- rowMeans(sapply(names(m_final), function(nm)
  as.numeric(dismo::predict(m_final[[nm]], as.data.frame(occ[, members[[nm]]$vars]), args = "outputformat=cloglog"))))
pred_check <- max(abs(p_occ - p_java))
```

```{r}
#| label: bootstrap
#| code-summary: "Show code: regenerate the 30 bootstrap replicates of the consensus"
fc_args <- function(fc) {
  f <- strsplit(fc, "")[[1]]
  c(paste0("linear=", "L" %in% f), paste0("quadratic=", "Q" %in% f), paste0("hinge=", "H" %in% f),
    paste0("product=", "P" %in% f), "threshold=false", "autofeature=false")
}
fit_mx <- function(p, a, vars, fc, rm) {
  x <- rbind(as.data.frame(p[, vars]), as.data.frame(a[, vars]))
  dismo::maxent(x = x, p = c(rep(1, nrow(p)), rep(0, nrow(a))),
                args = c(fc_args(fc), paste0("betamultiplier=", rm), "doclamp=true"))
}
cached("bootstrap", {
  refit_check <- all(map_lgl(names(members), function(nm) {
    cf <- members[[nm]]; identical(fit_mx(occ, bg_train, cf$vars, cf$fc, cf$rm)@lambdas, m_final[[nm]]@lambdas) }))
  n_boot <- 30
  set.seed(31)                                         # same resampling scheme and seed as code_3
  boot_L <- map(seq_len(n_boot), function(b) {
    idx <- unlist(lapply(regs, function(r) { i <- which(occ$region == r); i[sample.int(length(i), replace = TRUE)] }))
    lapply(members, function(cf) parse_lambdas(fit_mx(occ[idx, ], bg_train, cf$vars, cf$fc, cf$rm)))
  })
}, c("refit_check", "boot_L", "n_boot"))
saveRDS(list(final = L_final, boot = boot_L, members = members, thr_p10 = thr_p10),
        file.path(proc_v7, "consensus_lambdas.rds"))
```

```{r}
#| label: projection-grid
#| code-summary: "Show code: projection domain, jurisdictions, known records, elevation"
cur_suit <- rast(file.path(proc_v6, "suitability_current_aus.tif"))    # code_6 current suitability (continental Australia + Tasmania)
env_au   <- mask(crop(env_all[[sel_vars]], cur_suit), cur_suit)
cells    <- which(!is.na(values(cur_suit)))
env_cur  <- as.data.frame(values(env_au)[cells, sel_vars])
p_cur    <- ens_pred(L_final, env_cur)
cur_check <- max(abs(p_cur - values(cur_suit)[cells]))
bin_cur  <- p_cur >= thr_p10
area_km2 <- values(cellSize(cur_suit, unit = "km"))[cells]
xy_cells <- xyFromCell(cur_suit, cells)
to_rast  <- function(v, nm = "value") { r <- rast(cur_suit); r[cells] <- v; names(r) <- nm; r }

# States and territories, as in code_6 (Lord Howe and Macquarie Islands are outside the projection domain)
jur <- ne_states(country = "Australia", returnclass = "sf") |>
  filter(!name %in% c("Lord Howe Island", "Macquarie Island")) |>
  mutate(jur = if_else(name == "Jervis Bay Territory", "New South Wales", name)) |>
  group_by(jur) |> summarise(geometry = st_union(geometry), .groups = "drop")
aus_sf <- jur
jur_r   <- rasterize(vect(jur), cur_suit, field = "jur")
jur_lv  <- levels(jur_r)[[1]]
jur_c   <- jur_lv$jur[match(values(jur_r)[cells], jur_lv[[1]])]
# cells not covered by the state polygons (coastal slivers) take the nearest jurisdiction
miss <- which(is.na(jur_c))
if (length(miss)) jur_c[miss] <- jur$jur[st_nearest_feature(st_as_sf(as.data.frame(xy_cells[miss, , drop = FALSE]), coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 4326), jur)]
jur_keep  <- names(which(c(tapply(area_km2, jur_c, sum)) > 1000))

# Known Australian records (training records plus georeferenced ALA records on Australian land), from code_6
known <- read_csv(file.path(proc_v6, "known_records_aus.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
known_cell <- unique(match(cellFromXY(cur_suit, as.matrix(known)), cells)); known_cell <- known_cell[!is.na(known_cell)]
dist_known <- values(mask(distance(cur_suit, vect(known, geom = c("lon", "lat"), crs = "EPSG:4326")) / 1000, cur_suit))[cells]

# Elevation (WorldClim 2.1, 2.5 arc-min) for elevational shift metrics
elev <- geodata::elevation_global(res = 2.5, path = file.path(base_dir, "data", "worldclim"))
elev_c <- terra::extract(elev, xy_cells)[[1]]

area_by <- function(w, g) c(tapply(area_km2 * w, g, sum, na.rm = TRUE))
cur_area_jur <- area_by(bin_cur, jur_c)
```

## Baseline species distribution model

All projections used the consensus model developed for current climate (`code_3`; projected to
Australia only in `code_6`), without refitting. The consensus is the unweighted mean cloglog output of three MaxEnt models, each pairing
annual mean temperature (BIO1) with moisture-supply and aridity predictors (set H: BIO1, BIO12, BIO15,
aridity; set C: BIO1, BIO2, BIO12, BIO15, aridity; set G: BIO1, BIO2, BIO13, BIO17, aridity). It was
calibrated on 389 thinned occurrence records from the native and invaded ranges with a
region-balanced target-group background, and it transferred well between continents (mean
leave-one-region-out AUC = 0.86; AUC = `r fmt(kr3$aus_eval$auc)` for Australian records when no Oceanian
records were used in training). Suitable climate was defined, as for current climate, by the 10th-percentile
training-presence threshold (cloglog = `r fmt(thr_p10, 3)`). Clamping was retained, as in calibration.

To make tens of thousands of projections tractable, predictions were computed directly from the
fitted MaxEnt feature weights (lambdas). This reproduces the MaxEnt Java output to within
`r formatC(pred_check, format = "e", digits = 0)` and reproduces the published current-climate map
exactly (maximum difference `r formatC(cur_check, format = "e", digits = 0)`). To represent
uncertainty in the SDM itself, the 30 bootstrap replicates of the code_3 consensus (presence records
resampled with replacement within regions; all three members refitted) were regenerated with the
same seed. Refitting the final model from the stored inputs reproduced the code_3 models exactly.

```{r}
#| label: future-climate
#| code-summary: "Show code: GCM ensemble, download and derivation of future predictors"
gcm_meta <- tribble(
  ~gcm,            ~centre,                       ~ecs, ~core, ~v2,
  "ACCESS-CM2",    "CSIRO-ARCCSS (Australia)",     4.7,  TRUE,  TRUE,
  "ACCESS-ESM1-5", "CSIRO (Australia)",            3.9,  TRUE,  FALSE,
  "CMCC-ESM2",     "CMCC (Italy)",                 3.6,  TRUE,  FALSE,
  "CNRM-ESM2-1",   "CNRM-CERFACS (France)",        4.8,  TRUE,  FALSE,
  "EC-Earth3-Veg", "EC-Earth Consortium (Europe)", 4.3,  TRUE,  FALSE,
  "GISS-E2-1-G",   "NASA GISS (USA)",              2.7,  TRUE,  FALSE,
  "IPSL-CM6A-LR",  "IPSL (France)",                4.6,  TRUE,  FALSE,
  "MIROC6",        "MIROC (Japan)",                2.6,  TRUE,  TRUE,
  "MPI-ESM1-2-HR", "MPI-M (Germany)",              3.0,  TRUE,  TRUE,
  "MRI-ESM2-0",    "MRI (Japan)",                  3.2,  TRUE,  FALSE,
  "UKESM1-0-LL",   "MOHC-NERC (UK)",               5.3,  FALSE, TRUE,
  "CNRM-CM6-1",    "CNRM-CERFACS (France)",        4.8,  FALSE, TRUE) |>
  mutate(likely = core & ecs >= 2.5 & ecs <= 4)          # within the IPCC AR6 'likely' ECS range
gcm_core <- gcm_meta$gcm[gcm_meta$core]
scen <- bind_rows(
  expand_grid(gcm = gcm_core, ssp = ssps, period = periods, set = "core"),
  expand_grid(gcm = c("UKESM1-0-LL", "CNRM-CM6-1"), ssp = c("245", "585"),
              period = c("2041-2060", "2081-2100"), set = "v2_only")) |>
  mutate(id = sprintf("%s_ssp%s_%s", gcm, ssp, period), file = file.path(fut_dir, paste0(id, ".tif")),
         ssp_l = factor(ssp_lab[ssp], levels = ssp_lab), period = factor(period, levels = periods))

# Future stacks are shared with code_4 (Australia/NZ grid; same 2.5' global grid), so they are cropped to the
# Australian projection grid before cell indexing
read_fut <- function(f, v = sel_vars) as.data.frame(values(crop(rast(f), cur_suit))[cells, v])
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(as.vector(ext(crop(rast(scen$file[1]), cur_suit))), as.vector(ext(cur_suit)))))
# Bioclimatic variables (WorldClim/dismo definitions) from cells x 12 monthly matrices
bioclim_m <- function(pr, tn, tx) {
  p1 <- pr + 1
  q  <- sapply(1:12, function(m) rowSums(pr[, ((m - 1 + 0:2) %% 12) + 1]))        # rolling 3-month totals
  cbind(bio1  = rowMeans((tn + tx) / 2),
        bio2  = rowMeans(tx - tn),
        bio12 = rowSums(pr),
        bio13 = do.call(pmax, as.data.frame(pr)),
        bio15 = 100 * sqrt(rowSums((p1 - rowMeans(p1))^2) / 11) / rowMeans(p1),
        bio17 = do.call(pmin, as.data.frame(q)))
}
# Thornthwaite aridity index (envirem::aridityIndexThornthwaite) with Hargreaves PET (envirem::monthlyPET);
# extraterrestrial radiation by latitude and month as in ENVIREM (envirem:::calcSolRad, year = 40)
lat_rows <- yFromRow(cur_suit, 1:nrow(cur_suit))
RA <- sapply(1:12, function(m) sapply(lat_rows, function(y) envirem:::calcSolRad(year = 40, lat = y, month = m)))
RA_m <- RA[rowFromCell(cur_suit, cells), ]
aridity_m <- function(pr, tn, tx) {
  pet <- 0.0023 * (RA_m * 30) * ((tn + tx) / 2 + 17.8) * sqrt(tx - tn)
  pet[pet < 0] <- 0
  dry <- pr < pet
  n <- rowSums(pet * dry); d <- rowSums((pet - pr) * dry)
  ifelse(n == 0, 0, 100 * d / n)
}
read_monthly <- function(f) values(crop(rast(f), cur_suit))[cells, ]
wc_dir <- file.path(base_dir, "data", "worldclim", "climate", "wc2.1_2.5m")
cur_m  <- lapply(c(pr = "prec", tn = "tmin", tx = "tmax"), function(v)
  read_monthly(file.path(wc_dir, sprintf("wc2.1_2.5m_%s_%02d.tif", v, 1:12))))
ai_wc21_cur <- aridity_m(cur_m$pr, cur_m$tn, cur_m$tx)                   # current, same formulation
ai_envirem  <- values(crop(env_all[["aridity_idx"]], cur_suit))[cells]  # ENVIREM baseline used in training
fut_vars <- c("bio1", "bio2", "bio12", "bio13", "bio15", "bio17", "aridity_idx")
# Socket workers / download code: see code_4 (prep_future_climate.R or the embedded chunk)
todo <- which(!file.exists(scen$file))
if (length(todo)) stop("Future predictor stacks missing in data/future_climate_cmip6/: run code_4/prep_future_climate.R first ",
                       "(stacks are shared with code_4 and use its Australia/NZ grid).")
stopifnot(all(file.exists(scen$file)))

# Validation of derived predictors against the layers used to train the model (current climate)
bc_cur  <- bioclim_m(cur_m$pr, cur_m$tn, cur_m$tx)
bc_val  <- map_dfr(colnames(bc_cur), ~ tibble(variable = .x, r = cor(bc_cur[, .x], env_cur[[.x]]),
                                              max_abs_diff = max(abs(bc_cur[, .x] - env_cur[[.x]]))))
ai_cor  <- cor(ai_envirem, ai_wc21_cur)
ai_bias <- quantile(ai_wc21_cur - ai_envirem, c(0.05, 0.5, 0.95))
# Check against the envirem implementation, supplying correctly oriented radiation layers
w_chk  <- ext(145, 151, -40, -33)
rd_chk <- function(v, nm) { r <- crop(rast(file.path(wc_dir, sprintf("wc2.1_2.5m_%s_%02d.tif", v, 1:12))), w_chk); names(r) <- paste0(nm, 1:12); r }
tn_c <- rd_chk("tmin", "tmin_"); tx_c <- rd_chk("tmax", "tmax_"); pr_c <- rd_chk("prec", "precip_")
lat_c <- yFromRow(tn_c, 1:nrow(tn_c))
ra_c <- rast(lapply(1:12, function(m) init(tn_c[[1]], fun = rep(sapply(lat_c, function(y) envirem:::calcSolRad(40, y, m)), each = ncol(tn_c)))))
names(ra_c) <- sprintf("et_solrad_%02d", 1:12); tm_c <- (tn_c + tx_c) / 2; names(tm_c) <- paste0("tmean_", 1:12)
pet_c <- envirem::monthlyPET(tm_c, ra_c, tx_c - tn_c)
ai_pkg <- envirem::aridityIndexThornthwaite(pr_c, pet_c)
k_chk <- match(cellFromXY(cur_suit, xyFromCell(ai_pkg, 1:ncell(ai_pkg))), cells)
envirem_check <- max(abs(ai_wc21_cur[k_chk] - values(ai_pkg)[, 1]), na.rm = TRUE)
```

## Future climate scenarios

Future monthly minimum and maximum temperature and precipitation were obtained from the WorldClim 2.1
CMIP6 downscaled projections at 2.5 arc-minutes [@fick2017; @eyring2016]. These are calibrated against
the same 1970–2000 WorldClim baseline used to train the model, so changes in the bioclimatic variables
are internally consistent with the training data. We used four SSPs spanning low to very high
emissions, SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, SSP3-7.0 and SSP5-8.5 [@oneill2016], and four 20-year periods:
2021–2040, 2041–2060, 2061–2080 and 2081–2100.

GCMs were selected using three criteria. (i) Monthly temperature and precipitation had to be
available for all SSP × period combinations; this excluded GFDL-ESM4. (ii) ECS had to lie within the
IPCC AR6 very likely range of 2–5 K [@forster2021; @meehl2020; @zelinka2020]; this excluded
UKESM1-0-LL (ECS ≈ 5.3 K) and INM-CM5-0 (≈ 1.9 K). (iii) Only one model per modelling centre and model
family was retained, to limit dependence among ensemble members [@knutti2017]; this excluded
CNRM-CM6-1 in favour of CNRM-ESM2-1. The two Australian ACCESS models were both kept because they
differ in their atmosphere and land components and are the national reference models for Australian
projections [@grose2020]. The resulting core ensemble has ten GCMs (@tbl-gcm), giving 160
GCM × SSP × period combinations. For sensitivity analyses we defined a "likely-ECS" subset of the six
core models with ECS of 2.5–4 K, and we also reproduced the five-GCM ensemble of the previous analysis,
which includes UKESM1-0-LL and CNRM-CM6-1.

BIO1, BIO2, BIO12, BIO13, BIO15 and BIO17 were computed from the monthly data using the WorldClim
definitions. Applied to current monthly climate, this reproduces the WorldClim 2.1 bioclimatic layers
used in training exactly (maximum difference < 10⁻⁵). The Thornthwaite aridity index
[@thornthwaite1948] was computed as in ENVIREM [@title2018]: 100 × the annual sum of monthly
water deficits (PET − P in months with P < PET) divided by the sum of PET in those months, with
monthly PET from the Hargreaves equation [@hargreaves1985] and extraterrestrial radiation by latitude
and month.^[We computed extraterrestrial radiation directly with `envirem:::calcSolRad()`.
`envirem::ETsolradRasters()` (version 3.1) assigns radiation by column rather than by row when used
with `terra`, so it varies with longitude on non-square grids. With correctly oriented radiation,
our implementation reproduces `envirem::monthlyPET()` and `envirem::aridityIndexThornthwaite()` to
within `r formatC(envirem_check, format = "e", digits = 0)`.] The aridity layer used in training is
the published ENVIREM layer, which is based on an earlier WorldClim baseline. The same index
recomputed from WorldClim 2.1 is closely correlated with it (r = `r fmt(ai_cor, 3)`) but not identical
(90% of differences between `r fmt(ai_bias[1], 1)` and `r fmt(ai_bias[3], 1)` index units;
@suppfig-validation a). We therefore applied the future change as an anomaly: future aridity =
ENVIREM aridity + (aridity from future monthly climate − aridity from WorldClim 2.1 current monthly
climate), bounded to the index range 0–100. Future aridity is thus derived from each GCM's own
temperature and precipitation and anchored to the training baseline.

## Projection, range change and spread metrics

The consensus model was projected to each of the 160 scenarios across the land area of continental
Australia and Tasmania (the projection domain of `code_6`). For each SSP × period combination we computed the ensemble median of suitability across
GCMs and, for each cell, the proportion of GCMs projecting suitable climate ("agreement"). Cells
suitable now were classified as *stable* if at least half of the GCMs projected them to remain
suitable, and as *lost* otherwise. Cells unsuitable now were classified as *gained* if at least half
of the GCMs projected them to become suitable. Changes were labelled *robust* when at least 80% of
GCMs agreed. Areas were computed from true, latitude-dependent cell areas. Area metrics are reported
as the median and range across the ten GCMs, computed from each GCM's own binary projection rather
than from the ensemble-median map. For each scenario we also calculated the proportion of grid cells
containing a known Australian record (training records and ALA records; `r length(known_cell)` cells)
that remained suitable. We also calculated the shift in the area-weighted latitude centroid and the
mean elevation of suitable climate.

## Extrapolation and clamping

Future climates were compared with the calibration environments (presence and training-background
points) in two ways. Univariate novelty was measured with the multivariate environmental similarity
surface (MESS < 0) [@elith2010], as for current climate. Novel combinations of individually analogue
values were measured with the ExDet NT2 statistic [@mesgaran2014]: the Mahalanobis distance of a cell
from the centroid of the reference data, divided by the maximum distance within the reference data
(NT2 > 1 indicates a novel combination). Because the model was fitted with clamping, predictions
for values beyond the training range are held at the edge of the fitted response. We quantified how
much this affects projections by comparing clamped and unclamped predictions. We report suitable
area both including and excluding cells with novel climate.

```{r}
#| label: extrapolation-functions
#| code-summary: "Show code: MESS and ExDet NT2"
# Reference environments for extrapolation diagnostics: presences + training background (as in code_3)
ref_env <- as.data.frame(bind_rows(occ[, sel_vars], bg_train[, sel_vars]))
ref_sorted <- lapply(ref_env, sort)
# MESS (Elith et al. 2010), vectorised; returns minimum similarity and the most dissimilar variable
mess_df <- function(x) {
  sim <- sapply(sel_vars, function(v) {
    r <- ref_sorted[[v]]; lo <- r[1]; hi <- r[length(r)]; p <- x[[v]]
    f <- 100 * findInterval(p, r, left.open = TRUE) / length(r)      # % of reference values < p
    ifelse(f == 0, 100 * (p - lo) / (hi - lo), ifelse(f <= 50, 2 * f, ifelse(f < 100, 2 * (100 - f), 100 * (hi - p) / (hi - lo))))
  })
  list(mess = apply(sim, 1, min), mod = sel_vars[apply(sim, 1, which.min)])
}
# ExDet NT2 (Mesgaran et al. 2014): Mahalanobis distance relative to the maximum within the reference data
ref_mu <- colMeans(ref_env); ref_S <- cov(ref_env)
d_ref_max <- sqrt(max(mahalanobis(ref_env, ref_mu, ref_S)))
nt2_df <- function(x) sqrt(mahalanobis(as.matrix(x[, sel_vars]), ref_mu, ref_S)) / d_ref_max
novelty <- function(x) { m <- mess_df(x); n2 <- nt2_df(x)
  list(cls = ifelse(m$mess < 0, 2L, ifelse(n2 > 1, 1L, 0L)), mess = m$mess, mod = m$mod) }   # 0 analogue, 1 combination, 2 univariate
nov_cur <- novelty(env_cur)
mess_check <- cor(nov_cur$mess, values(rast(file.path(proc_v6, "mess_current_aus.tif")))[cells], use = "complete")
```

```{r}
#| label: project-scenarios
#| code-summary: "Show code: project the consensus to all 168 scenarios"
# Project the consensus to every GCM x SSP x period; keep per-cell suitability (scaled integers) and novelty class,
# plus per-scenario summaries. Forked workers (no Java needed for lambda-based prediction).
swap <- function(base, fut, v) { base[v] <- fut[v]; base }
proj_one <- function(i) {
  x <- read_fut(scen$file[i])
  na <- !complete.cases(x)
  if (any(na)) x[na, ] <- env_cur[na, ]        # (coastal cells missing in the CMIP6 grid keep current climate)
  s   <- ens_pred(L_final, x)
  u   <- ens_pred(L_final, x, clamp = FALSE)
  s_t <- ens_pred(L_final, swap(env_cur, x, temp_vars))      # temperature change only
  s_m <- ens_pred(L_final, swap(env_cur, x, moist_vars))     # moisture change only
  nv  <- novelty(x)
  b <- s >= thr_p10
  w <- function(z, g) c(tapply(area_km2 * z, g, sum))
  summ <- bind_rows(lapply(list(all = rep("Australia", length(cells)), jur = jur_c), function(g)
    tibble(unit = names(w(b, g)), suitable = w(b, g), gain = w(b & !bin_cur, g), loss = w(!b & bin_cur, g),
           stable = w(b & bin_cur, g), suitable_analogue = w(b & nv$cls == 0, g),
           suitable_temp_only = w(s_t >= thr_p10, g), suitable_moist_only = w(s_m >= thr_p10, g),
           suitable_unclamped = w(u >= thr_p10, g), suitable_mss = w(s >= thr_mss, g),
           novel_univariate = w(nv$cls == 2, g), novel_combination = w(nv$cls == 1, g),
           clamp_affected = w(abs(s - u) > 0.05, g),
           lat_centroid = c(tapply(xy_cells[, 2] * area_km2 * b, g, sum)) / w(b, g),
           elev_mean = c(tapply(elev_c * area_km2 * b, g, sum, na.rm = TRUE)) / w(b, g),
           lat_centroid_w = c(tapply(xy_cells[, 2] * area_km2 * s, g, sum)) / w(s, g))))
  summ$known_suitable <- NA_real_; summ$known_suitable[1] <- mean(b[known_cell])
  wm <- function(z, k) sum(z[k] * area_km2[k]) / sum(area_km2[k])
  clim <- map_dfr(list(`Current suitable range` = bin_cur, `All land` = rep(TRUE, length(cells))), function(k)
    tibble(d_bio1 = wm(x$bio1 - env_cur$bio1, k), d_bio2 = wm(x$bio2 - env_cur$bio2, k),
           d_bio12_pct = 100 * (wm(x$bio12, k) / wm(env_cur$bio12, k) - 1),
           d_bio17_pct = 100 * (wm(x$bio17, k) / wm(env_cur$bio17, k) - 1),
           d_aridity = wm(x$aridity_idx - env_cur$aridity_idx, k)), .id = "domain") |> mutate(id = scen$id[i], .before = 1)
  summ$n_na <- sum(na)
  list(s = as.integer(round(s * 1e4)), cls = as.raw(nv$cls), summ = mutate(summ, id = scen$id[i], .before = 1), clim = clim)
}
cached("projections", {
  proj <- mclapply(seq_len(nrow(scen)), proj_one, mc.cores = n_cores, mc.preschedule = FALSE)
  S   <- sapply(proj, `[[`, "s");   colnames(S) <- scen$id          # suitability x 1e4
  NOV <- sapply(proj, `[[`, "cls"); colnames(NOV) <- scen$id
  summ_all <- bind_rows(lapply(proj, `[[`, "summ")) |> left_join(dplyr::select(scen, id, gcm, ssp, ssp_l, period, set), by = "id")
  clim_all <- bind_rows(lapply(proj, `[[`, "clim")) |> left_join(dplyr::select(scen, id, gcm, ssp, ssp_l, period, set), by = "id")
  rm(proj)
}, c("S", "NOV", "summ_all", "clim_all"))
```

```{r}
#| label: current-summaries
#| code-summary: "Show code: area summaries"
# Current-climate equivalents of the scenario summaries
w0 <- function(z, g) c(tapply(area_km2 * z, g, sum))
summ_cur <- bind_rows(lapply(list(all = rep("Australia", length(cells)), jur = jur_c), function(g)
  tibble(unit = names(w0(bin_cur, g)), suitable_cur = w0(bin_cur, g), suitable_mss_cur = w0(p_cur >= thr_mss, g),
         lat_centroid_cur = c(tapply(xy_cells[, 2] * area_km2 * bin_cur, g, sum)) / w0(bin_cur, g),
         elev_mean_cur = c(tapply(elev_c * area_km2 * bin_cur, g, sum, na.rm = TRUE)) / w0(bin_cur, g))))
summ_all <- summ_all |> left_join(summ_cur, by = "unit") |>
  mutate(pct_change = 100 * (suitable - suitable_cur) / suitable_cur,
         pct_change_mss = 100 * (suitable_mss - suitable_mss_cur) / suitable_mss_cur)
known_cur <- mean(bin_cur[known_cell])
write_csv(summ_all, file.path(out_dir, "scenario_summaries_all.csv"))

core <- filter(summ_all, set == "core")
ens_summ <- core |> group_by(unit, ssp, ssp_l, period) |>
  summarise(across(c(suitable, gain, loss, stable, pct_change, suitable_analogue, novel_univariate, novel_combination,
                     clamp_affected, known_suitable, lat_centroid, elev_mean, suitable_temp_only, suitable_moist_only,
                     pct_change_mss),
                   list(med = ~ median(.x, na.rm = TRUE), lo = ~ min(.x, na.rm = TRUE), hi = ~ max(.x, na.rm = TRUE))),
            .groups = "drop")
write_csv(ens_summ, file.path(out_dir, "ensemble_summaries.csv"))
```

```{r}
#| label: ensemble-maps
#| code-summary: "Show code: ensemble median, GCM agreement and change classes"
# Per SSP x period: ensemble-median suitability, fraction of GCMs projecting suitable, fraction novel
grp <- scen |> filter(set == "core") |> distinct(ssp, period) |> arrange(ssp, period)
ens_maps <- pmap(grp, function(ssp, period) {
  ids <- scen$id[scen$set == "core" & scen$ssp == ssp & scen$period == period]
  sm  <- S[, ids] / 1e4
  list(ssp = ssp, period = period,
       med   = matrixStats::rowMedians(sm),
       agree = rowMeans(sm >= thr_p10),
       novel = rowMeans(matrix(as.integer(NOV[, ids]), ncol = length(ids)) > 0),
       novel_uni = rowMeans(matrix(as.integer(NOV[, ids]), ncol = length(ids)) == 2),
       sd    = matrixStats::rowSds(sm))
})
names(ens_maps) <- sprintf("%s_%s", grp$ssp, grp$period)
# change class: 0 stable unsuitable, 1 loss (>=50% GCMs unsuitable), 2 stable suitable, 3 gain (>=50% GCMs suitable)
chg_class <- function(e) ifelse(bin_cur, ifelse(e$agree >= 0.5, 2L, 1L), ifelse(e$agree >= 0.5, 3L, 0L))
for (k in names(ens_maps)) {
  e <- ens_maps[[k]]
  writeRaster(c(to_rast(e$med, "median_suitability"), to_rast(e$agree, "gcm_agreement_suitable"),
                to_rast(e$sd, "gcm_sd"), to_rast(e$novel, "frac_gcm_novel"), to_rast(chg_class(e), "change_class")),
              file.path(proc_v7, sprintf("ensemble_ssp%s.tif", k)), overwrite = TRUE)
}
```

## Attribution of projected change

To determine which climatic changes drive the projected range shifts, each scenario was re-projected
with only the temperature predictors (BIO1, BIO2) changed to future values and the moisture
predictors held at current values, and vice versa. At finer resolution, for the two focal scenarios
(SSP2-4.5, 2041–2060; SSP3-7.0, 2081–2100), each predictor was changed singly. In cells classified as
lost or gained, the predictor whose individual change produced the largest decrease or increase in
suitability (ensemble median across GCMs) was mapped as the dominant driver.

```{r}
#| label: drivers
#| code-summary: "Show code: attribution of change to individual predictors"
# Attribution: substitute each predictor's future value singly (others at current) for the focal scenarios
cached("drivers", {
  drv <- map(focal, function(k) {
    ids <- scen$id[scen$set == "core" & sprintf("%s_%s", scen$ssp, scen$period) == k]
    per_gcm <- mclapply(ids, function(id) {
      x <- read_fut(scen$file[scen$id == id])
      na <- !complete.cases(x); if (any(na)) x[na, ] <- env_cur[na, ]
      list(d = sapply(sel_vars, function(v) ens_pred(L_final, swap(env_cur, x, v)) - p_cur), x = as.matrix(x),
           clamp = ens_pred(L_final, x) - ens_pred(L_final, x, clamp = FALSE))
    }, mc.cores = n_cores)
    arr <- simplify2array(lapply(per_gcm, `[[`, "d"))     # cells x vars x GCMs
    xa <- simplify2array(lapply(per_gcm, `[[`, "x"))
    x_med <- sapply(sel_vars, function(v) matrixStats::rowMedians(xa[, v, ]))
    list(delta_med = sapply(sel_vars, function(v) matrixStats::rowMedians(arr[, v, ])), x_med = x_med,
         clamp_med = matrixStats::rowMedians(sapply(per_gcm, `[[`, "clamp")),
         area_loss_single = apply(arr, c(2, 3), function(d) sum(area_km2 * (bin_cur & (p_cur + d) < thr_p10))),
         area_gain_single = apply(arr, c(2, 3), function(d) sum(area_km2 * (!bin_cur & (p_cur + d) >= thr_p10))))
  })
  names(drv) <- focal
}, c("drv"))
dom_driver <- function(k) {
  e <- ens_maps[[k]]; dm <- drv[[k]]$delta_med; cl <- chg_class(e)
  out <- rep(NA_integer_, length(cells))
  out[cl == 1] <- apply(dm[cl == 1, , drop = FALSE], 1, which.min)
  out[cl == 3] <- apply(dm[cl == 3, , drop = FALSE], 1, which.max)
  out
}
drv_tab <- map_dfr(focal, function(k) {
  tibble(scenario = k, variable = sel_vars,
         loss_med = apply(drv[[k]]$area_loss_single, 1, median), gain_med = apply(drv[[k]]$area_gain_single, 1, median))
})
```

## Partitioning of uncertainty

For each period, every bootstrap replicate of the consensus was projected to every GCM and SSP
(4 SSPs × 10 GCMs × 30 replicates = 1,200 projections per period). Change in suitable area was
computed relative to each replicate's own current-climate projection and threshold. The variance in
projected percentage change was partitioned by analysis of variance into main effects of emissions
scenario, GCM and SDM replicate, and their interactions [@dinizfilho2009; @buisson2010]. For the
focal scenarios we also mapped the standard deviation of suitability among GCMs (final model) and
among SDM replicates (averaged across GCMs).

```{r}
#| label: bootstrap-projection
#| code-summary: "Show code: project every bootstrap replicate to every scenario"
# SDM (parameter) uncertainty: every bootstrap consensus projected to every core scenario.
# Area change is computed relative to each replicate's own current-climate projection.
cached("bootstrap_projections", {
  cur_boot <- sapply(boot_L, function(Lb) { s <- ens_pred(Lb, env_cur); thr <- unname(quantile(ens_pred(Lb, occ), 0.10))
    c(thr = thr, all = sum(area_km2 * (s >= thr))) })
  thr_boot <- cur_boot["thr", ]
  core_idx <- which(scen$set == "core")
  boot_one <- function(i) {
    x <- read_fut(scen$file[i])
    na <- !complete.cases(x); if (any(na)) x[na, ] <- env_cur[na, ]
    sb <- sapply(seq_along(boot_L), function(b) ens_pred(boot_L[[b]], x))
    bb <- sweep(sb, 2, thr_boot, ">=")
    ar <- rbind(all = colSums(area_km2 * bb))
    key <- sprintf("%s_%s", scen$ssp[i], scen$period[i])
    list(id = scen$id[i], area = ar, sd = if (key %in% focal) apply(sb, 1, sd) else NULL)
  }
  bproj <- mclapply(core_idx, boot_one, mc.cores = n_cores, mc.preschedule = FALSE)
  boot_area <- map_dfr(bproj, function(z) as_tibble(t(z$area)) |> mutate(id = z$id, boot = seq_len(n_boot))) |>
    transmute(id, boot, unit = "Australia", suitable = all) |>
    left_join(tibble(boot = seq_len(n_boot), suitable_cur = cur_boot["all", ]), by = "boot") |>
    mutate(pct_change = 100 * (suitable - suitable_cur) / suitable_cur) |>
    left_join(dplyr::select(scen, id, gcm, ssp, ssp_l, period), by = "id")
  sdm_sd <- lapply(focal, function(k) { ids <- scen$id[core_idx][sprintf("%s_%s", scen$ssp[core_idx], scen$period[core_idx]) == k]
    rowMeans(sapply(Filter(function(z) z$id %in% ids, bproj), `[[`, "sd")) })
  names(sdm_sd) <- focal
  rm(bproj)
}, c("cur_boot", "thr_boot", "boot_area", "sdm_sd", "core_idx"))
write_csv(boot_area, file.path(out_dir, "bootstrap_scenario_areas.csv"))
```

```{r}
#| label: variance-partition
#| code-summary: "Show code: ANOVA partitioning of uncertainty"
# Partition of variance in projected % change in suitable area among emissions scenario, GCM and SDM (bootstrap)
vp <- boot_area |> group_by(unit, period) |> group_modify(function(d, k) {
  a <- anova(lm(pct_change ~ ssp_l * gcm + ssp_l * factor(boot) + gcm * factor(boot), data = d))
  ss <- setNames(a$`Sum Sq`, rownames(a))
  tibble(component = c("Emissions scenario (SSP)", "Climate model (GCM)", "SDM parameters (bootstrap)", "Interactions"),
         ss = c(ss["ssp_l"], ss["gcm"], ss["factor(boot)"], sum(ss[grepl(":", names(ss))]) + ss["Residuals"])) |>
    mutate(frac = ss / sum(ss))
}) |> ungroup()
write_csv(vp, file.path(out_dir, "variance_partitioning.csv"))
```

## Management categories

To support surveillance planning, cells were classified by current suitability and GCM agreement
into: *persistent* (suitable now; ≥ 80% of GCMs suitable in future), *at risk* (suitable now; 20–80%),
*likely loss* (suitable now; ≤ 20%), *emerging, robust* (unsuitable now; ≥ 80%), *emerging, possible*
(unsuitable now; 50–80%) and *unsuitable*. Emerging areas more than 100 km from any known record were
identified as candidate areas for anticipatory surveillance.

## Sensitivity analyses

We compared projected change in suitable area obtained with (i) the core ensemble, (ii) the
likely-ECS subset and (iii) the five-GCM ensemble of the previous analysis, for the scenarios and
periods used previously (SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5; 2041–2060 and 2081–2100). We also recomputed area
change using the threshold that maximises sensitivity plus specificity (cloglog =
`r fmt(thr_mss, 3)`), which was used in the previous analysis.

```{r}
#| label: v2-comparison
#| code-summary: "Show code: quantify problems in the previous analysis"
# (1) v2 delta-change aridity vs physically derived aridity, for the two v2 stacks that bracket the scenario range
v2_cmp <- map_dfr(c("MPI-ESM1-2-HR_ssp245_2041-2060", "ACCESS-CM2_ssp585_2081-2100"), function(id) {
  v2 <- rast(file.path(base_dir, "data", "future_climate", paste0(id, "_all_selected.tif")))
  v2 <- resample(crop(v2, cur_suit), cur_suit, method = "near")
  v4 <- crop(rast(file.path(fut_dir, paste0(id, ".tif"))), cur_suit)
  tibble(id = id, cell = cells, v2 = values(v2[["aridity_idx"]])[cells, 1],
         v4 = values(v4[["aridity_idx"]])[cells, 1], current = env_cur$aridity_idx)
}) |> drop_na()
v2_ai_stats <- v2_cmp |> group_by(id) |>
  summarise(pct_above_100 = 100 * mean(v2 > 100), max_v2 = max(v2), max_v4 = max(v4),
            mean_change_v2 = mean(v2 - current), mean_change_v4 = mean(v4 - current),
            pct_outside_train_v2 = 100 * mean(v2 > max(ref_env$aridity_idx)),
            pct_outside_train_v4 = 100 * mean(v4 > max(ref_env$aridity_idx)))
# (2) Area bias of the single-latitude cell-area approximation used in v2
area_v2_approx <- sum(bin_cur) * prod(res(cur_suit)) * 111^2 * cos(mean(ext(cur_suit)[3:4]) * pi / 180)
area_true <- sum(area_km2 * bin_cur)
# (3) Sensitivity of projected change to the GCM ensemble (all with the code_3 consensus)
gcm_sets <- list(`Core ensemble (10 GCMs)` = gcm_core, `Likely-ECS subset (6 GCMs)` = gcm_meta$gcm[gcm_meta$likely],
                 `v2 ensemble (5 GCMs)` = gcm_meta$gcm[gcm_meta$v2])
set_cmp <- imap_dfr(gcm_sets, function(g, nm) summ_all |>
  filter(unit == "Australia", gcm %in% g, ssp %in% c("245", "585"), period %in% c("2041-2060", "2081-2100")) |>
  group_by(ssp_l, period) |> summarise(n = n(), med = median(pct_change), lo = min(pct_change), hi = max(pct_change), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(ensemble = nm))
v2_res <- read_csv(file.path(base_dir, "outputs_2", "per_gcm_results_v2.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
v2_loro <- read_csv(file.path(base_dir, "outputs_2", "loro_cv_results_v2.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
v2_unc <- read_csv(file.path(base_dir, "outputs_2", "ensemble_uncertainty_v2.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
thr_cmp <- core |> filter(unit == "Australia", ssp %in% c("245", "585"), period %in% c("2041-2060", "2081-2100")) |>
  group_by(ssp_l, period) |> summarise(n = n(), med = median(pct_change_mss), lo = min(pct_change_mss), hi = max(pct_change_mss), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(ensemble = "Core ensemble, MSS threshold")
v2_cur_area <- read_csv(file.path(base_dir, "outputs_2", "range_shift_summary_v2.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)$current_suitable_km2[1]
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-helpers
#| code-summary: "Show code: plotting helpers"
map_base <- list(coord_sf(xlim = c(112.5, 154), ylim = c(-44, -9.5), expand = FALSE),
                 labs(x = NULL, y = NULL),
                 theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#f4f8fb", colour = NA),
                       axis.text = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank()))
# Long data frame of cell values for faceted maps (aggregated 2x for plotting)
map_df <- function(vals, keys, fact = 2, fun = "mean") {
  imap_dfr(vals, function(v, k) {
    r <- to_rast(v); if (fact > 1) r <- aggregate(r, fact, fun = fun, na.rm = TRUE)
    as.data.frame(r, xy = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE) |> mutate(key = k)
  }) |> left_join(keys, by = "key")
}
key_lab <- function(k) tibble(key = k, ssp_l = factor(ssp_lab[sub("_.*", "", k)], levels = ssp_lab),
                              period = factor(sub(".*_", "", k), levels = periods))
known_pts <- known                                        # records on Australian land (code_6)
```

All analyses were run in R `r paste(R.version$major, R.version$minor, sep = ".")` using `terra`
`r packageVersion("terra")`, `sf`, `dismo` `r packageVersion("dismo")` (bundled MaxEnt 3.4), `envirem`
`r packageVersion("envirem")`, `predicts` and the `tidyverse`.

# Results

```{r}
#| label: results-values
#| include: false
mns <- function(x, d = 0) sub("^-", "−", formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d))
sgn <- function(x) sub("^-", "−", sprintf("%+.0f", x))
es  <- function(u, s, p) filter(ens_summ, unit == u, ssp == s, period == p)
pc  <- function(u, s, p) { e <- es(u, s, p); sprintf("%s%% (GCM range %s to %s%%)", sgn(e$pct_change_med), sgn(e$pct_change_lo), sgn(e$pct_change_hi)) }
pcm <- function(u, s, p) sgn(es(u, s, p)$pct_change_med)
kn  <- function(s, p) fmt(100 * es("Australia", s, p)$known_suitable_med, 0)
cl  <- function(s, p, v = "d_bio1", f = median) f(filter(clim_all, set == "core", domain == "Current suitable range", ssp == s, period == p)[[v]])
att <- core |> filter(unit == "Australia") |>
  mutate(t = 100 * (suitable_temp_only - suitable_cur) / suitable_cur, m = 100 * (suitable_moist_only - suitable_cur) / suitable_cur) |>
  group_by(ssp, period) |> summarise(t = median(t), m = median(m), c = median(pct_change), .groups = "drop")
at  <- function(s, p, v) filter(att, ssp == s, period == p)[[v]]
vpv <- function(u, p, comp) 100 * filter(vp, unit == u, period == p, component == comp)$frac
sc  <- function(nm, s, p) filter(set_cmp, ensemble == nm, ssp_l == ssp_lab[s], period == p)$med
dl  <- function(k, v, what = "loss_med") filter(drv_tab, scenario == k, variable == v)[[what]] / 1000
mg  <- function(k, u, cls) { x <- filter(mg_area, scenario == k, unit == u, class == cls)$area; if (length(x)) x / 1000 else 0 }
loss_tot <- function(k) { s <- sub("_.*", "", k); p <- sub(".*_", "", k); es("Australia", s, p)$loss_med / 1000 }
au_lat <- function(s) median(filter(core, unit == "Australia", ssp == s, period == "2081-2100")$lat_centroid -
                               filter(core, unit == "Australia", ssp == s, period == "2081-2100")$lat_centroid_cur)
au_el  <- function(s) median(filter(core, unit == "Australia", ssp == s, period == "2081-2100")$elev_mean -
                               filter(core, unit == "Australia", ssp == s, period == "2081-2100")$elev_mean_cur)
ex <- ens_summ |> filter(unit == "Australia")
```

## Problems in the previous analysis and their effects

The re-examination identified thirteen problems (@supptbl-v2). The most consequential was the
derivation of future aridity. The ratio-based delta change produced aridity values above the
theoretical maximum of the index in `r fmt(v2_ai_stats$pct_above_100[v2_ai_stats$id == "MPI-ESM1-2-HR_ssp245_2041-2060"], 0)`%
of Australian land under MPI-ESM1-2-HR SSP2-4.5 2041–2060 and in
`r fmt(v2_ai_stats$pct_above_100[v2_ai_stats$id == "ACCESS-CM2_ssp585_2081-2100"], 0)`% under ACCESS-CM2
SSP5-8.5 2081–2100, where values reached `r fmt(v2_ai_stats$max_v2[v2_ai_stats$id == "ACCESS-CM2_ssp585_2081-2100"], 0)`
(@suppfig-validation b). In the second scenario the mean increase in aridity was
`r fmt(v2_ai_stats$mean_change_v2[v2_ai_stats$id == "ACCESS-CM2_ssp585_2081-2100"], 1)` index units under the v2
method but `r fmt(v2_ai_stats$mean_change_v4[v2_ai_stats$id == "ACCESS-CM2_ssp585_2081-2100"], 1)` units when
aridity was derived from the same GCM's monthly climate. With the v2 method,
`r fmt(v2_ai_stats$pct_outside_train_v2[v2_ai_stats$id == "ACCESS-CM2_ssp585_2081-2100"], 0)`% of cells
had aridity beyond the calibration range; with the corrected method, none did. This artefact,
not climate change, accounts for most of the 60–81% extrapolation reported previously. The model
projected in v2 also failed to transfer between regions under current climate (leave-one-region-out
AUC = `r fmt(v2_loro$auc[v2_loro$region == "Oceania"])` for Oceania), so its future projections had no
demonstrated predictive basis. The single-latitude cell-area approximation overestimated suitable
area by `r fmt(100 * (area_v2_approx / area_true - 1), 0)`% for the current map. Including the three
high-sensitivity GCMs of the v2 ensemble inflated projected losses relative to the core ensemble,
most at the end of the century (SSP2-4.5 2081–2100: `r sgn(sc("v2 ensemble (5 GCMs)", "245", "2081-2100"))`%
vs. `r sgn(sc("Core ensemble (10 GCMs)", "245", "2081-2100"))`%; @supptbl-sens, @suppfig-sens).

## Projected climate change across the current range

Across the current suitable range, every GCM projects warming in every scenario (@tbl-gcm,
@fig-climate). By 2021–2040, annual mean temperature is about `r fmt(cl("245", "2021-2040"), 1)` °C above the
1970–2000 baseline in all SSPs, which is essentially the warming that has already occurred. By
2081–2100 the ensemble-median warming is `r fmt(cl("126", "2081-2100"), 1)` °C (SSP1-2.6),
`r fmt(cl("245", "2081-2100"), 1)` °C (SSP2-4.5), `r fmt(cl("370", "2081-2100"), 1)` °C (SSP3-7.0) and
`r fmt(cl("585", "2081-2100"), 1)` °C (SSP5-8.5), with a GCM range of about ±1 °C around each median.
Projected changes in annual precipitation are small and of inconsistent sign (ensemble medians
`r sgn(cl("126", "2081-2100", "d_bio12_pct"))` to `r sgn(cl("585", "2081-2100", "d_bio12_pct"))`%; GCM range
`r sgn(min(filter(clim_all, set == "core", domain == "Current suitable range")$d_bio12_pct))` to
`r sgn(max(filter(clim_all, set == "core", domain == "Current suitable range")$d_bio12_pct))`%). The aridity index
nevertheless increases in almost all GCM × scenario combinations (median
`r fmt(cl("245", "2041-2060", "d_aridity"), 1)` units by 2041–2060 under SSP2-4.5 and
`r fmt(cl("585", "2081-2100", "d_aridity"), 1)` units by 2081–2100 under SSP5-8.5), because evaporative
demand rises with temperature while rainfall changes little. Change in diurnal temperature range is
negligible (< 0.5 °C). The greatest warming is projected for inland and northern Australia, and the
least for Tasmania and the south-east coast (@suppfig-climmaps).

## Future suitability and range change

Projected change is dominated by contraction of suitable climate at the warm and dry margins of the
Australian range; gains elsewhere are small (@fig-future-suit, @fig-change, @tbl-change). Suitable
area changes by `r pc("Australia", "245", "2041-2060")` by 2041–2060 under SSP2-4.5. By 2081–2100 the
change is `r pcm("Australia", "126", "2081-2100")`% under SSP1-2.6, `r pcm("Australia", "245", "2081-2100")`%
under SSP2-4.5, `r pc("Australia", "370", "2081-2100")` under SSP3-7.0 and
`r pcm("Australia", "585", "2081-2100")`% under SSP5-8.5. Total gains are small in every scenario
(≤ `r fmt(max(ex$gain_med) / 1000, 0)` × 10³ km²) compared with losses of up to
`r fmt(max(ex$loss_med) / 1000, 0)` × 10³ km².

Losses are concentrated where the tick's range already approaches its thermal and moisture limits
(@fig-change, @tbl-jur): coastal and subcoastal Queensland, the northern rivers and western slopes
of New South Wales, inland and western Victoria, south-eastern South Australia and south-western
Western Australia. Queensland and Western Australia lose most of their suitable area: Queensland
`r sgn(es("Queensland", "245", "2041-2060")$pct_change_med)`% by 2041–2060 under SSP2-4.5 and
`r sgn(es("Queensland", "370", "2081-2100")$pct_change_med)`% by 2081–2100 under SSP3-7.0; Western Australia
`r sgn(es("Western Australia", "245", "2041-2060")$pct_change_med)`% and
`r sgn(es("Western Australia", "370", "2081-2100")$pct_change_med)`%, respectively. New South Wales, which has
the largest suitable area, changes by `r sgn(es("New South Wales", "245", "2041-2060")$pct_change_med)`% by
2041–2060 under SSP2-4.5 and `r sgn(es("New South Wales", "370", "2081-2100")$pct_change_med)`% by 2081–2100
under SSP3-7.0, and Victoria by `r sgn(es("Victoria", "245", "2041-2060")$pct_change_med)`% and
`r sgn(es("Victoria", "370", "2081-2100")$pct_change_med)`%. Tasmania (`r sgn(es("Tasmania", "370", "2081-2100")$pct_change_med)`%
by 2081–2100 under SSP3-7.0) is almost entirely stable. As a result,
the suitable area in Australia contracts towards the south-east and to higher ground: by 2081–2100 its
area-weighted centroid moves `r fmt(abs(au_lat("245")), 1)`° (SSP2-4.5) to `r fmt(abs(au_lat("585")), 1)`°
(SSP5-8.5) poleward, and its mean elevation rises by `r fmt(au_el("245"), 0)`–`r fmt(au_el("585"), 0)` m
(@suppfig-shift). Individual GCMs agree on the spatial pattern of losses and differ mainly in their
extent (@suppfig-pergcm).

## Trajectories and the fate of known localities

Losses in Australia accumulate steadily (@fig-trajectory a). A large part of the projected
contraction has already occurred by 2021–2040 (`r pcm("Australia", "245", "2021-2040")`% under SSP2-4.5),
when the four SSPs are still indistinguishable. The scenarios diverge after mid-century: under
SSP1-2.6 losses stabilise at about `r mns(-es("Australia", "126", "2081-2100")$pct_change_med)`%, whereas under SSP3-7.0 and
SSP5-8.5 they continue to grow to the end of the century. Of the grid cells with known records of
the tick in Australia, `r fmt(100 * known_cur, 0)`% are climatically suitable under
the 1970–2000 baseline. This falls to `r kn("245", "2041-2060")`% by 2041–2060 under SSP2-4.5 and to
`r kn("126", "2081-2100")`%, `r kn("245", "2081-2100")`%, `r kn("370", "2081-2100")`% and `r kn("585", "2081-2100")`%
by 2081–2100 under SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, SSP3-7.0 and SSP5-8.5 (@fig-trajectory b). The localities
that become unsuitable are mostly in south-east Queensland and northern New South Wales.

::: {.primary-figure}
```{r}
#| label: fig-trajectory
#| fig-cap: "(a) Change in climatically suitable area through the century relative to 1970–2000. Lines are medians across ten GCMs; ribbons span the GCM range. (b) Percentage of grid cells with known Australian records of *H. longicornis* that remain climatically suitable."
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 4.8
traj <- core |> filter(unit == "Australia") |>
  group_by(unit, ssp_l, period) |>
  summarise(med = median(pct_change), lo = min(pct_change), hi = max(pct_change),
            q1 = quantile(pct_change, 0.25), q3 = quantile(pct_change, 0.75), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(year = per_mid[as.character(period)])
traj0 <- bind_rows(traj, expand_grid(unit = "Australia", ssp_l = factor(ssp_lab, levels = ssp_lab)) |>
  mutate(med = 0, lo = 0, hi = 0, q1 = 0, q3 = 0, year = 1985))
p_tr <- ggplot(traj0, aes(year, med, colour = ssp_l, fill = ssp_l)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.12, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) + geom_point(size = 1.4) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = ssp_col, name = NULL) + scale_fill_manual(values = ssp_col, name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1985, per_mid), labels = c("1970–\n2000", gsub("-", "–\n", periods))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Change in suitable area (%)", tag = "a") + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
kn <- core |> filter(unit == "Australia") |> group_by(ssp_l, period) |>
  summarise(med = 100 * median(known_suitable), lo = 100 * min(known_suitable), hi = 100 * max(known_suitable), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(year = per_mid[as.character(period)]) |>
  bind_rows(tibble(ssp_l = factor(ssp_lab, levels = ssp_lab), med = 100 * known_cur, lo = 100 * known_cur, hi = 100 * known_cur, year = 1985))
p_kn <- ggplot(kn, aes(year, med, colour = ssp_l, fill = ssp_l)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.12, colour = NA) + geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) + geom_point(size = 1.4) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = ssp_col, guide = "none") + scale_fill_manual(values = ssp_col, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1985, per_mid), labels = c("1970–\n2000", gsub("-", "–\n", periods))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Known localities climatically suitable (%)", tag = "b")
p_tr + p_kn + plot_layout(widths = c(1.2, 1))
save_fig("Fig4_trajectories", w = 13, h = 4.8)
```
:::

## Climatic drivers of change

Warming is the main driver of projected losses (@fig-drivers). In Australia, changing only the
temperature predictors reduced suitable area by `r mns(-at("245", "2041-2060", "t"))`% by 2041–2060 under
SSP2-4.5 and by `r mns(-at("370", "2081-2100", "t"))`% by 2081–2100 under SSP3-7.0. Changing only the moisture
predictors reduced it by `r mns(-at("245", "2041-2060", "m"))`% and `r mns(-at("370", "2081-2100", "m"))`%,
respectively, against combined losses of `r mns(-at("245", "2041-2060", "c"))`% and
`r mns(-at("370", "2081-2100", "c"))`%. Most of the moisture effect comes from the aridity index
(@supptbl-drivers), which itself increases mainly because warming raises evaporative demand.
Precipitation variables alone have little effect. Warming acting alone would remove
`r fmt(dl("370_2081-2100", "bio1"), 0)` × 10³ km² of currently suitable climate by 2081–2100 under
SSP3-7.0, increased aridity alone `r fmt(dl("370_2081-2100", "aridity_idx"), 0)` × 10³ km² and the change in
diurnal range alone `r fmt(dl("370_2081-2100", "bio2"), 0)` × 10³ km². Rising annual mean temperature is
the dominant driver of loss along the Queensland and New South Wales coast and ranges. Increasing
aridity and diurnal range dominate along the southern margin of the range in Victoria, South
Australia, south-western Western Australia and parts of the Tasmanian midlands (@fig-drivers b,
@suppfig-drivervars).

::: {.primary-figure}
```{r}
#| label: fig-drivers
#| fig-cap: "Climatic drivers of projected change. (a) Change in suitable area when only the temperature predictors (BIO1, BIO2), only the moisture predictors (BIO12, BIO13, BIO15, BIO17, aridity) or all predictors are changed to future values (bars: median across GCMs; whiskers: range). (b) Dominant driver in cells projected to be lost or gained (the predictor whose individual change most decreases or increases suitability; ensemble median) for SSP2-4.5 2041–2060 and SSP3-7.0 2081–2100. Losses are coloured by their dominant driver; the few gained cells are shown in green."
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 9
att <- core |> filter(unit == "Australia", period %in% c("2041-2060", "2081-2100")) |>
  transmute(unit, ssp_l, period, gcm, `Temperature only` = 100 * (suitable_temp_only - suitable_cur) / suitable_cur,
            `Moisture only` = 100 * (suitable_moist_only - suitable_cur) / suitable_cur, `Combined` = pct_change) |>
  pivot_longer(c(`Temperature only`, `Moisture only`, Combined), names_to = "driver") |>
  mutate(driver = factor(driver, levels = c("Temperature only", "Moisture only", "Combined"))) |>
  group_by(unit, ssp_l, period, driver) |> summarise(med = median(value), lo = min(value), hi = max(value), .groups = "drop")
p_att <- ggplot(att, aes(ssp_l, med, fill = driver)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(0.8), width = 0.75) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), position = position_dodge(0.8), width = 0.25, linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Temperature only" = "#d6604d", "Moisture only" = "#4393c3", Combined = "grey35"), name = NULL) +
  facet_grid(~ period) + labs(x = NULL, y = "Change in suitable area (%)", tag = "a") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
drv_col <- setNames(c("#e41a1c", "#ff7f00", "#4daf4a", "#a6d854", "#377eb8", "#984ea3", "#a65628"), var_lab[sel_vars])
drv_loss <- function(k) { d <- dom_driver(k); cl <- chg_class(ens_maps[[k]]); ifelse(cl == 3, 99L, ifelse(cl == 1, d, NA_integer_)) }
d_drv <- map_df(setNames(lapply(focal, drv_loss), focal), key_lab(focal), fun = "modal") |>
  mutate(drv = factor(ifelse(value == 99, "Gain (any driver)", paste("Loss:", var_lab[sel_vars][pmin(value, 7)])),
                      levels = c(paste("Loss:", var_lab[sel_vars]), "Gain (any driver)")),
         panel = paste(ssp_l, period))
p_dm <- ggplot(d_drv) +
  geom_sf(data = aus_sf, fill = "grey92", colour = NA) +
  geom_raster(aes(x, y, fill = drv)) +
  geom_sf(data = aus_sf, fill = NA, colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(setNames(drv_col, paste("Loss:", names(drv_col))), "Gain (any driver)" = "#1b7837"),
                    name = NULL, drop = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~ panel) + map_base + labs(tag = "b") + theme(legend.position = "bottom") + guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
p_att / p_dm + plot_layout(heights = c(0.7, 1.15))
save_fig("Fig5_drivers", w = 13, h = 9)
```
:::

## Extrapolation and sources of uncertainty

Future climates outside the calibration range are extensive but confined to areas that are
unsuitable in any case. Univariate novelty (MESS < 0), driven almost entirely by annual mean
temperature exceeding the warmest calibration conditions, covers
`r fmt(100 * min(ex$novel_univariate_med) / sum(area_km2), 0)`–`r fmt(100 * max(ex$novel_univariate_med) / sum(area_km2), 0)`%
of the land area, all of it in tropical and arid northern Australia (@suppfig-novelty,
@supptbl-extrap). No cells had novel combinations of individually analogue values (NT2 > 1), and
≥ `r fmt(100 * min(ex$suitable_analogue_med / ex$suitable_med), 1)`% of projected suitable area lies in
analogue climate in every scenario. Clamping changed suitability by more than 0.05 only in the hot
north, where suitability is far below the threshold. Projected range change therefore does not
depend on extrapolation.

The relative importance of uncertainty sources changes through the century (@fig-uncert a,
@supptbl-vp). For Australia, the GCM accounts for most of the variance in projected change until
mid-century (`r fmt(vpv("Australia", "2041-2060", "Climate model (GCM)"), 0)`% in 2041–2060), while the
emissions scenario accounts for only `r fmt(vpv("Australia", "2041-2060", "Emissions scenario (SSP)"), 0)`%.
By 2081–2100 the emissions scenario is the largest source
(`r fmt(vpv("Australia", "2081-2100", "Emissions scenario (SSP)"), 0)`%), followed by the GCM
(`r fmt(vpv("Australia", "2081-2100", "Climate model (GCM)"), 0)`%). Uncertainty in the SDM itself
contributes `r fmt(vpv("Australia", "2081-2100", "SDM parameters (bootstrap)"), 0)`–`r fmt(vpv("Australia", "2041-2060", "SDM parameters (bootstrap)"), 0)`%.
Spatially, GCM uncertainty is highest along the coast and ranges of south-east
Queensland and northern New South Wales, where the projected losses occur. SDM uncertainty is
lower and more evenly spread (@fig-uncert b, @suppfig-sdmgcm). Excluding the GCMs with ECS above
4 K changed projected losses by at most two percentage points (@suppfig-sens), and the MSS threshold
gave slightly smaller losses than the 10th-percentile threshold
(SSP2-4.5 2081–2100: `r sgn(filter(thr_cmp, ssp_l == "SSP2-4.5", period == "2081-2100")$med)`% vs.
`r sgn(sc("Core ensemble (10 GCMs)", "245", "2081-2100"))`%).

::: {.primary-figure}
```{r}
#| label: fig-uncert
#| fig-cap: "Sources of uncertainty in projections. (a) Partitioning of the variance in projected percentage change in suitable area among emissions scenario, GCM, SDM bootstrap replicate and their interactions (4 SSPs × 10 GCMs × 30 replicates per period). (b) Standard deviation of projected suitability among GCMs (final consensus) and among SDM bootstrap replicates (averaged over GCMs), SSP3-7.0 2081–2100."
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 5.5
p_vp <- vp |>
  mutate(component = factor(component, levels = rev(c("Emissions scenario (SSP)", "Climate model (GCM)", "SDM parameters (bootstrap)", "Interactions")))) |>
  ggplot(aes(period, 100 * frac, fill = component)) + geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Emissions scenario (SSP)" = "#E71D25", "Climate model (GCM)" = "#4393c3",
                               "SDM parameters (bootstrap)" = "#5aae61", "Interactions" = "grey75"), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = function(x) gsub("-", "–", x)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Variance in projected change (%)", tag = "a") + theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, reverse = TRUE))
k_u <- "370_2081-2100"
d_unc <- bind_rows(
  as.data.frame(aggregate(to_rast(ens_maps[[k_u]]$sd), 2, mean, na.rm = TRUE), xy = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE) |> mutate(src = "Among climate models (GCM SD)"),
  as.data.frame(aggregate(to_rast(sdm_sd[[k_u]]), 2, mean, na.rm = TRUE), xy = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE) |> mutate(src = "Among SDM bootstrap replicates (SD)"))
p_unc <- ggplot(d_unc) + geom_raster(aes(x, y, fill = value)) +
  geom_sf(data = aus_sf, fill = NA, colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.1) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "viridis", name = "SD of\nsuitability", limits = c(0, NA)) +
  facet_wrap(~ src) + map_base + labs(tag = "b")
p_vp + p_unc + plot_layout(widths = c(1, 2.4))
save_fig("Fig6_uncertainty", w = 13, h = 5.5)
```
:::

::: {.primary-figure}
```{r}
#| label: fig-surv
#| fig-cap: "Management categories derived from current suitability and GCM agreement for a mid-century moderate-emissions scenario (SSP2-4.5 2041–2060) and an end-of-century high-emissions scenario (SSP3-7.0 2081–2100). *Persistent*: suitable now and in ≥ 80% of GCMs; *at risk*: suitable now and in 20–80%; *likely loss*: suitable now and in ≤ 20%; *emerging (robust)*: unsuitable now, suitable in ≥ 80%; *emerging (possible)*: 50–80%. Black points are known records; lines are state and territory boundaries."
#| fig-width: 13

mg_lab <- c("Unsuitable", "Emerging (possible)", "Emerging (robust)", "Persistent (robust)", "At risk (uncertain)", "Likely loss")
mg_col <- setNames(c("grey90", "#c2a5cf", "#762a83", "#1b7837", "#fdb863", "#d73027"), mg_lab)
mgmt <- function(e) { f <- e$agree
  ifelse(bin_cur, ifelse(f >= 0.8, 4L, ifelse(f <= 0.2, 6L, 5L)), ifelse(f >= 0.8, 3L, ifelse(f >= 0.5, 2L, 1L))) }
d_mg <- map_df(setNames(lapply(ens_maps[focal], mgmt), focal), key_lab(focal), fun = "modal") |>

ggplot(d_mg) + geom_raster(aes(x, y, fill = cls)) +

mg_area <- map_dfr(focal, function(k) { m <- mgmt(ens_maps[[k]])
```
